 Learn more Like the up-and-down motions of the aircraft it's trying to build, Archer Aviation (NYSE: ACHR) has dropped vertically in 2026. It started the year at about $8 a share. It now trades at less than $4. 
 Of course, no one said this would be easy: Archer is trying to build a business in an industry that is still taking shape. It is also working hard to certify a new type of aircraft -- an electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) craft -- whose commercial potential remains largely untested. 
 Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » 
 So, down over 50%, is Archer a compelling buy? 
 Image source: Archer Aviation. For certain investors, maybe. The thing is, Archer is still years away from proving it can turn its electric air taxis into a profitable business. The keyword there is "prove": We still don't know how many people will pay to fly across a city, or whether fares will leave much room for profits once maintenance and operation costs become clear. On top of that, we also don't know how many aircraft Archer can reliably produce, or what their costs will be. 
 At the same time, these problems aren't irresolvable. But they will take time to solve, and not every investor will likely have the time horizon -- or patience -- to remain invested while the uncertainties linger. 
 So, the long and the short of it: If you want a radically new form of transportation -- flying taxis -- to replace sitting in a car in traffic, and you can stay invested for a long period, Archer at today's price might be a compelling buy. But if volatility and the possibility of losing your investment would keep you up at night, this stock is probably worth passing on.
